tagline: The Eagles lose 4 games and win a sixth straight title anyway, 40-26 over the Bengals in Super Bowl CLV, Ryland Maxwell takes a 7th Super Bowl MVP at 34 and re-signs with Akiem Brock for one more run, and Grover Calitro scores 43 times.

articles.headline: Six Straight: Eagles Beat the Bengals 40-26 in Super Bowl CLV
articles.dek: Philadelphia lost 4 regular-season games, its most under Dorren Skura, and still won a sixth straight title as Ryland Maxwell took a 7th Super Bowl MVP at 34.
body: The losses came, and the trophy came anyway. Dorren Skura's Eagles went 13-4 in Y96, the most regular-season defeats in his nine seasons in Philadelphia, after records of 17-0, 15-2 and 17-0 in the three years before. Then they beat the Bengals 40-26 in Super Bowl CLV, the 155th edition of the game, for the club's sixth straight championship.

The core never left the field. Ryland Maxwell, Bones Crawford, Akiem Brock and Calvin Wingo II each played all 21 of Philadelphia's games, playoffs included. Maxwell ran for 2,574 yards, the most in the league. Crawford threw 52 touchdown passes, also the most. Wingo led every receiver with 2,096 yards, and Brock made 62 blocks when no other lineman made more than 33.

Cincinnati arrived with the hottest runner in the league. Grover Calitro had scored 43 rushing touchdowns, the most in a season on league cards, and Alshon Lazard had turned his career back around. The Bengals put up 26 points in the final. Philadelphia scored 40.

It was not a farewell. Maxwell, 34, won his 13th ring and was named Super Bowl MVP for the 7th time. Brock, also 34, won his 8th ring, and Crawford won his 8th as well. Then the runner and the blocker who had been on the field for every title of the run both re-signed with Skura for one more year, and they open Y97 at 35. The question for the rest of the league is an old one: how to beat this team while its two constants are still on the field.

articles.headline: Mad Max at 34: 2,574 Yards, a 7th Super Bowl MVP and One More Year
articles.dek: Ryland Maxwell's Y96 was one of his best. He has 32,108 career rushing yards, 13 rings and the highest Career Legacy on file, and he re-signed for Y97.
body: Most great runners fade at 34. Ryland Maxwell sped up. He ran for 2,574 yards, 670 more than anyone else in the league, and scored 25 rushing touchdowns in 21 games. He stands at 32,108 career yards, the league record, 7,601 clear of Lane McCoy's 24,507.

The touchdown list is the one race he has not won yet. Maxwell's 421 rushing touchdowns top Skura's record board but rank third in the league, 4 behind Siran Spector's 425 and 37 behind McCoy's 458. Everything else is already his: 125 career touchdown catches, 13 rings and 7 Super Bowl MVPs, the last two both the most on file.

His Career Legacy stands at 14,903, the highest on file, and the Hall of Fame watch scores him at 100, the maximum, far above the bar of 65. The Hall will have to wait. Skura re-signed him in Y96, and he opens Y97 at 35, still an Eagle. Every one of his rings came with Dorren Skura: 2 with the Jets, 5 with the Falcons and 6 with the Eagles. One ordinary season would carry him past Spector, and few backs have ever been given the chance to try at 35.

articles.headline: Akiem Brock Has 8 Rings, a Hall of Fame Case and One More Year to Play
articles.dek: The league's best blocker made 62 blocks in Y96 at 34, and he and Ryland Maxwell are both back for another run.
body: No lineman on league cards came near Akiem Brock in Y96, and none had for years. He made 62 blocks in 21 games, 29 more than JD Pircher of the Bengals or Caleb Linsley of the Giants, and passed 500 for his career on the way to 538 in 181 games.

He spent his whole card career in Philadelphia, and the rings followed: 8 of them, every one with Dorren Skura. In nine seasons together, Skura's Eagles won the title eight times. Y90 was the one that got away.

The Hall of Fame watch scores him at 79, the best standing among offensive linemen and well clear of the bar of 65; Maxwell's is 100, the maximum. His Career Legacy stands at 11,394 and his card at 29,312. He was 34 in Y96, the same age as Maxwell, and both re-signed with Skura to play Y97 at 35. Linemen rarely get the headlines in a dynasty built on a record-setting runner and a quarterback who threw 52 touchdown passes in Y96. When the vote does come, it will say what the box scores never could: the runner and the quarterback had help.

articles.headline: Leglue's MVP at 36 Is a Verdict on Crawford's 17 Interceptions
articles.dek: Bones Crawford threw 52 touchdown passes, 11 more than anyone, and led the league in interceptions for a third straight season. The award went to Detroit.
body: Margus Leglue has spent his whole card career in Detroit, and at 36 he finally won the league's top award. He threw for 3,803 yards and 41 touchdowns with 1 interception in 19 games and was named Most Valuable Player for the first time. His overall rose from 78 to 84 and his card from 237 to 874.

The case against Bones Crawford made itself. He threw 52 touchdown passes, the most in the league, and 17 interceptions, when no other quarterback threw more than 6. It was the third season in a row he led the league in interceptions, after 20 in Y94 and 10 in Y95, and this time the voters held it against him. His MVP count stays at 5.

The market took the other side. Crawford's card value rose 124.4% to 19,210, and he collected his 8th ring. Leglue has the trophy; Crawford has the jewellery and the price tag. One of them was the better quarterback in Y96, and the argument will outlast both careers.

articles.headline: Calitro's 43 Touchdowns Break the Season Mark and Carry Cincinnati to the Final
articles.dek: Grover Calitro passed Siran Spector's 42 for the most rushing touchdowns in a season on file, and Alshon Lazard found his game again. The Bengals fell 40-26 in Super Bowl CLV.
body: Two seasons ago Cincinnati went 6-11 and its young quarterback was a cautionary tale. In Y96 the Bengals were the last club standing between the Eagles and a sixth straight title, and they lost Super Bowl CLV 40-26.

Grover Calitro was the reason they got there. He ran for 1,904 yards, second only to Ryland Maxwell, and scored 43 rushing touchdowns, the most in a single season on league cards, one more than Siran Spector's 42 for Houston in Y89. Nobody else in the league scored more than 30. He played all 21 games.

Alshon Lazard threw 39 touchdown passes as a rookie in Y93 and fell to 18 a year later. In Y96 he found the middle: 3,749 yards, 33 touchdowns and 2 interceptions. Teair Dye, in his second season, made 225 tackles.

The critics will point to what Calitro did not win. The Offensive Player of the Year award went to Alton Yeldon of the Seahawks, who ran for 1,558 yards and 27 touchdowns. A record season and no trophy: Cincinnati will take the trip to the final instead.

articles.headline: Brooker Draws Level With Hobbs at 43, and Swaim Climbs to Third on the Tackle List
articles.dek: Jamon Brooker tied the career interception record, Lewis Pettis was shut out, and Ryland Maxwell sits 4 rushing touchdowns short of second place.
body: A year ago Jamon Brooker and Lewis Pettis were tied at 41 interceptions, 2 short of Damar Hobbs. Brooker got both in Y96. He picked off 2 passes for the Packers and now shares the career record of 43 with Hobbs. At 33, he needs one more to own it.
Pettis played all 17 of the Cowboys' games and did not intercept a pass. He stays at 41, though his overall still rose from 95 to 97.

Travon Swaim made 199 tackles for the Lions and reached 3,064, passing Kyron Atwell's 3,059 for third on the career list. Only K'Lavon Settle, at 3,185, and Terron Stidham, at 3,132, have more, and Swaim is 121 from the record.

Angelo Moton of the Packers scored 30 rushing touchdowns and passed 350 for his career. And the chase still open: Maxwell is at 421, 4 short of Spector's 425 for second on that list, and he is back for Y97.

articles.headline: Ty Lock's Long Goodbye, and the Rookie Who Took His Place
articles.dek: The Giants' quarterback since Y83 is retired after 330 games and 627 touchdown passes. Yurik Okudah threw 34 in his first season.
body: Ty Lock's retirement is now on the record, and his last snaps came in Y95, when he was 39. He played 330 games, threw for 68,237 yards and 627 touchdowns with 137 interceptions, and won 2 MVP awards. Both of his rings came early, with Dorren Skura's Jets, before a multi-team trade sent him to New York ahead of Y83.
New York was his home for thirteen seasons and never gave him a ring. From Y88 on, the obstacle was his old coach: by the end of Y95 the Giants had met Skura's Eagles 17 times and lost all 17.

His successor arrived ready. Yurik Okudah, a rookie, threw for 3,610 yards and 34 touchdowns with 2 interceptions in 19 games. His card sells for 23, the price of an unknown, but the market's skill grade already reads A+. Lock spent a career chasing Philadelphia. Okudah has time to start his own chase.

articles.headline: Rashawn Elder Catches 122 Passes, and the Class of Y95 Keeps Coming
articles.dek: A rookie tight end led the league in catches, Mario Lamb scored 28 times for the Chiefs, and Payton Jarrett has 2 rings in 2 seasons.
body: Twenty-one new players reached league cards in Y96. The busiest was Rashawn Elder of the Colts, a tight end who caught 122 passes, the most in the league, though for only 675 yards, 5.5 a catch. Mario Lamb ran for 1,463 yards and 28 touchdowns for the Chiefs, Damiere Norton threw 28 touchdown passes for the Patriots, and Rico Gee threw 25 with 1 interception for the Cowboys.

Last year's class did not slow down. Bryant Herbig threw 30 touchdown passes for the Commanders for the second straight season, Teair Dye made 225 tackles for the Bengals, and tight end Ulysees Howell caught 81 passes.

Payton Jarrett had the best of it again: 74 catches, 1,419 yards and 16 touchdowns, second in the league in receiving yards behind Calvin Wingo II for the second year running, and a 2nd ring in his 2nd season. His overall rose from 67 to 72 and his card from 13 to 37. It is still a bargain.

articles.headline: Quick Hits
articles.dek: A second Defensive Player of the Year award, a tight end's leap and a linebacker who led the league in sacks.
body: Abraham Jack of the Bills was Defensive Player of the Year for the 2nd time, with 237 tackles, tied with A.T. Hoyer of the Raiders for the most.
Alton Yeldon of the Seahawks was Offensive Player of the Year for the first time.
Jacob Proise's overall jumped from 84 to 93 and his card from 1,109 to 5,527 after 786 yards and 14 touchdown catches.
Snoop Dotson led the league with 4 sacks and 2 forced fumbles, added 5 interceptions and won his 7th ring.
Lenny Baun of the Dolphins intercepted 6 passes, the most in the league.
Calvin Wingo II caught 104 passes for 2,096 yards and 18 touchdowns, the most receiving yards in the league for a second straight season.
Koa Zuber, "Uber Feasts", won his 7th ring with 131 tackles and 2 interceptions.
